entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad, Lucknow Bench
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Heard Sri Shamshad Ahmad Khan, learned counsel for the applicant, Sri Manoj Kumar Sahu, the
learned Aga for the State and perused the record.

2.  The present bail application has been filed by the applicant with the prayer to enlarge him on bail in Case Crime No. 119 of 2022, under Sections 376, 504, 506 IPC, Police Station Haiderganj, District Faizabad/Ayodhya.

3. The aforesaid case has been registered on the basis of an FIR lodged on 29.05.2022, in furtherance of an application under Section 156(3) Cr.P.C. filed on 05.05.2022, stating that for the past two years, the applicant repetitively made physical relations with the informant under a false promise of marrying her but subsequently the applicant declined to marry her.

The informant's father got her married with another person on 22.04.2022, she went to her marital home on 23.04.2022 and on the same day, the applicant went to the informant's marital home, abused the informant and told her in-laws that the informant was his concubine.

Due to the aforesaid conduct Krishna Kumar Yadav vs State Of U.P. Thru.Prin.Secy.Home on 22 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/154806140/
1 of the applicant, the informant's husband and his family members turned the informant out of her matrimonial home.

entities.text: Krishna Kumar Yadav vs State Of U.P. Thru.Prin.Secy.Home
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 4. The learned counsel for the applicant has submitted that the FIR does not contain any specific date and time of alleged incident and that the FIR had been lodged after two years since the alleged occurrence.
He has further submitted that the allegations are not supported by the medico legal examination report of the victim.
5. Learned AGA has opposed the prayer for bail but he could not dispute the aforesaid aspects of the matter.

6. Having considered the aforesaid facts and circumstances of the case what prima facie appears from the material placed before the Court at this stage is that in the statements of the victim recorded under Sections 161 & 164 Cr.P.C., she consistently stated that the applicant forcibly made physical relations with her and when she resisted, the applicant stated that he would marry her but subsequently, he declined to marry the informant and when her father got her married to another parson, the applicant went to her matrimonial home, misbehaved with her resulting in she being turned out of her matrimonial home.

7. Having considered the aforesaid facts and circumstances of the case and keeping in view the fact that the informant's stand is consistent in the application under Section 156(3) Cr.P.C., in the statements given before the Investigating Officer as well as before the Magistrate; that when the informant's father got her married and she went to her matrimonial home on 23.04.2022, the applicant went to the informant's matrimonial home on 23.04.2022 itself and conducted himself in such a manner resulting in the informant being turned out from matrimonial home, I am of the view that the aforesaid facts do not warrant exercise of discretion of this court by enlarging the applicant on bail.
8. Accordingly, this bail application stands rejected.

Order Date :- 22.5.2023 Pradeep/-
